subject: Eden Chang
intro: Hi, I'm Eden, a technical product manager.

My projects often begin where someone gets stuck: finding the right information, following a shared process, or choosing a tool for the job. I work through what they need and how the pieces fit together, then use diagrams and prototypes to explore a clearer way forward.

experience.name: Understand the situation
experience.description: Start with what someone is trying to do, what they already know, and where they need help. Different roles often need different paths through the same information.

experience.name: Work through the awkward parts
experience.description: Missing information, permissions and interrupted steps all affect the experience. I use workflows and diagrams to make those decisions explicit.

experience.name: Give the idea a form
experience.description: Prototypes make a proposed experience easier to examine. They help me spot gaps, reconsider the scope and work through practical constraints.

strengths.name: Problem framing
strengths.description: Sort through scattered requirements to clarify what needs solving.

strengths.name: Empathy
strengths.description: Understand what people need before deciding what to build.

strengths.name: Cross-functional communication
strengths.description: Help users, business and engineering agree on a plan.

strengths.name: Structured thinking
strengths.description: Work out the workflows, priorities and next steps behind an idea.

headline: Make the next
step clearer.

perspective.heading: A design perspective
paragraphs: My design background taught me to think about how something fits into a person's surroundings and routines.
That perspective now shapes how I organize information, plan interactions and work through system behavior.
